D002-D013_h008.question_both:
I’ve been struggling for maybe a few months now… it’s hard to say exactly when it started, it just kind of crept up.

With work, I’ll open a project, and the second I see a long timeline or a detailed brief, I just feel this mental wall. I put it off, scroll on my phone, or suddenly decide I need to reorganize my folders instead. Even when a client is talking to me on Zoom, I’ll realize halfway through that I tuned out and have no idea what they just said, even though I’m looking right at them. It’s not that I don’t care; it’s like my brain drifts without asking me.

I misplace stuff constantly—SD cards, my headphones, that little dongle I need for my laptop. I’ll set them down “for a second” and then spend twenty minutes tearing the place apart.

On top of that, my motivation’s been low. I feel kind of flat, like it takes more effort than it should just to get started on anything, even things I used to enjoy editing. Some days I just feel tired and kind of weighed down, and then my focus is even worse, but I can’t tell what’s causing what.
D002-D013_h008.question_a:
It’s mainly that my brain just doesn’t stay put, and it’s been like this as long as I can remember, way before I ever felt “down.” My mom used to complain I’d “zone out” in the middle of her talking to me, and that still happens now with clients on Zoom — they’re telling me what they want in the video and halfway through I realize I’ve missed chunks of what they said, even though I’m looking right at them.

Anything that takes steady focus, like editing long clips or going through detailed briefs, I put off or bounce in and out of. I’ll open Premiere, do five minutes, then suddenly I’m checking my phone or wandering to the kitchen. It’s not because I’m sad in that moment; it’s just exhausting to hold my attention in one place.

I’m always misplacing stuff I need — SD cards, hard drives, even my headphones — and then I’m late or miss deadlines. Lately I’ve also been feeling more low and unmotivated, kind of guilty and tired a lot of the time, but the spacing out and losing things were there way before this mood stuff started.
D002-D013_h008.question_b:
I’ve been feeling really low for about the past two months, like someone turned the dimmer down on everything. Around the same time this started, my ability to focus just crashed. Before this, I could sit for hours editing and actually kind of get lost in it. Now, as soon as I open a project, my brain just fogs up and I want to shut my laptop.

When people talk to me—my mom, clients on Zoom—I catch myself zoning out halfway through. They’ll finish and I realize I didn’t actually take in what they said, even though I was looking right at them. It’s not like this was an issue before I started feeling this down; it all came on together.

I’ve also started misplacing my stuff a lot lately—hard drives, my tablet pen, even my headphones. I’ll set them down and then wander around the apartment frustrated, trying to remember where I put them. I avoid starting edits that need a lot of mental effort, let emails pile up, and then feel guilty and more depressed, which makes it even harder to concentrate.

On the road, dispatch will give me a set of instructions, and I’ll start out fine, then somewhere along the way I realize I’ve skipped a stop or mixed up which load was supposed to go where. It’s not like I’m trying to ignore them; it just kind of slips past me.

I keep misplacing stuff I need for work—my logbook, bills of lading, even my handheld and fuel cards. I’ll set them down in the cab or at a truck stop and then spend 20 minutes tearing everything apart looking for them. Same thing at home: keys, mail, important papers, they end up who knows where.

I’m also forgetting basic things more than I used to—calling my kids back when I said I would, paying a bill until I get a late notice, missing a doctor’s appointment because it just left my head. Along with that, I’ve been feeling pretty low and worn out, not really enjoying much, especially on my days off. I can’t tell if the mood stuff is making it harder to focus, or if the constant screwups are what’s dragging me down.
D002-D013_h024.question_a:

Even back in grade school, teachers were always on me for “not finishing what I start.” I’d get halfway through worksheets or chores at home and then just… drift off or forget what I was doing. That’s still happening now with my routes and paperwork. I’ll start the logbook or a delivery checklist, then get distracted, and next thing I know I’ve skipped steps or left things incomplete.

I’m always misplacing stuff I need for work—keys, fuel cards, bills of lading, even my phone. I set something down in the cab, then I’m tearing it apart ten minutes later because I can’t remember where I put it. I also constantly forget everyday things—calling my kids back, keeping appointments, picking up things my ex asks me to grab for the kids. The low mood and feeling down have been worse since the divorce, but the spacey, scattered feeling and trouble focusing were there long before that and don’t really change much with how sad I’m feeling.
D002-D013_h024.question_b:

I feel down most days, heavy, like everything’s pointless. Around the same time that started, I began losing track of what I’m supposed to be doing. My dispatcher will give me clear instructions, and I’ll zone out halfway through. I’ll miss a step, forget a drop-off detail, or not finish the paperwork he asked for. That wasn’t happening before I started feeling this low.

I keep misplacing basic stuff—fuel cards, delivery receipts, even my logbook. I’ll put something down in the cab and five minutes later I can’t find it. I’m also forgetting everyday things: calling my kids back when I said I would, paying my phone bill on time, or showing up late to maintenance appointments. 

What’s strange is, when my mood briefly lifts for a day or two, my concentration is pretty much back to normal. It’s only when I’m in this dark, low state that my attention really falls apart.

I’ve noticed at work I’ll get instructions for a project, I’ll nod along, maybe even write some of it down, but when I sit back at my desk I can’t seem to carry it through the way I was told. I’m misplacing things a lot more, too—my calculator, client files, even my glasses. I’ll put a folder down “just for a second” and then spend 20 minutes hunting for it. At home, I forget small things constantly: paying a bill on time, calling someone back, switching the laundry, appointments I’d agreed to. My husband will say, “We talked about this,” and I honestly don’t remember.

At the same time, I just feel… weighed down. Low energy, not much interest in anything after work, like I’m moving through molasses. I can’t tell if I’m having trouble focusing because I feel down, or if feeling down is coming from messing things up so much.
D002-D013_h025.question_a:
I’ve always been a bit scatterbrained, even as a kid. My teachers used to write on my report cards that I “don’t finish what she starts.” That’s kind of followed me my whole life. At work now, as an accountant, I’ll start on a client file and then get sidetracked by an email or another pile of papers, and suddenly the original task is half-done and buried. My manager has had to remind me a few times about missing pieces in reports, and it’s embarrassing at my age.

I’m constantly misplacing things I need—my reading glasses, calculator, USB drives, even important receipts. I’ll set something down while I’m thinking about another task and then have no idea where I put it. At home, I forget to pay bills on time, or I’ll agree to an appointment and then completely miss it unless my husband reminds me.

The low mood and feeling “down” have been more on and off the last few years, but the trouble focusing and finishing things has been there as long as I can remember, even in times when my mood felt okay.
D002-D013_h025.question_b:
It’s really only been in these last four months that everything has started to slip. Before that, I was always the organized one—my job as an accountant kind of depends on it. But since I started feeling so low and drained, my mind just doesn’t seem to work the same.

At the office, my boss gives me instructions and I’ll nod along, but when I sit back down, it’s like my brain hits a wall. I reread emails over and over and still can’t make myself finish reports I used to breeze through. It’s not that I don’t care; I feel weighed down and hopeless, and then I just stall out.

I’ve started misplacing basic things—my glasses, client folders, even my calculator—which is very unlike me. At home, I forget simple things like paying the electric bill on time, calling people back, or keeping doctor’s appointments. My husband keeps asking what’s wrong because this all began around the same time I lost interest in everything and started waking up exhausted and tearful most mornings. When my mood dips, the fogginess and forgetfulness get much worse; on the rare better day, I can focus almost like I used to.
